text: Shared panel base and colour helpers of the anchor writer scripts. What: panel_type() returns AnchorPanel , the non-modal PythonQt panel of the Anchors scripts: script controls, a live preview table, Reload selection, Close and Apply. ink , muted and readable_palette give readable text colours in FontLab's light and dark themes. ERROR_COLOR colours blocked rows; MAX_ROWS limits the preview rows. How: the panel plans with fontlabapp.anchors.writer ( collect , blocked_rows , require_safe ) on every control change, and Apply plans again from live data and writes with anchor_writer.apply_work (one Undo step). Signals connect through scripting.connect_guarded and disconnect in closeEvent . Why: the seven Anchors scripts then hold only their planner, a small panel subclass and main . This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules at load time; PythonQt loads inside the functions, and panel_type() loads the class from fontlabapp.anchors.panel.ui . So FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast, and tests without Qt can import it. Offline tests do not prove native panel behaviour. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.anchors.panel.model as anchor_panel class RoundToGrid(anchor_panel.panel_type()): TITLE, KEY, ACTION = "Round Anchors to Grid", "anchors_round_to_grid", "Round" def build_controls(self): ... def planner(self): ...

text: Non-modal panel: script controls, live preview table, Reload, Close, Apply. What: a subclass sets TITLE , KEY , ACTION (the Apply button text) and HEADERS (3 or 4 columns), and fills in build_controls and planner . Optional hooks: chosen_masters , glyph_names and on_reload . Helpers for subclasses: watch , spin , scope_box . How: every control change recomputes the plan from the live font and shows exactly what Apply would write. Apply stays off while any row is blocked or require_safe refuses. Apply binds to the font, master and glyphs of the last scan, plans again, scans the auto-layer facts again and writes once through anchor_writer.apply_work . Why: the preview can never be stale at Apply, and an exception in a slot stays in the status line instead of reaching FontLab. Show it with scripting.show_script_dialog(Subclass, Subclass.KEY) .

text: apply_work ( work : Work , title : str , facts : AutoFacts ) -> dict [ str , Any ] Write all edits as ONE native Undo step named title . work holds no auto layer ( collect ); facts is a fresh history.scan_auto_facts . Call require_safe first. The commit uses history.commit(..., operation="geometry", read_back=...) . No rollback is tried: a failure after history started raises history.PartialWriteError with "use Edit > Undo". A value that FontLab did not keep raises history.unstored_error ("FontLab did not store ... Check those layers before you save."). Empty work returns zeros and makes no history call. Return {"anchors": native pin operations, "layers": edited layers} . One removed pin counts once, also for a repeated name.

text: Add plain components to EXISTING glyphs, inside the caller's one history step. What: a script that adds components to glyphs that exist (Make Lower Unicase, Set Default Figures) needs a new component shape for each (base glyph, layer). No component constructor is measured on this FontLab build (fl#8505: setGlyphComponents rejects every argument form, addComponent only records a recipe entry; the source has an flShape(glyph, layer) constructor, pyflshape.cpp:66-79 , which is a native probe item and is not used). Two calls: build_components(package, target, wanted, facts) , BEFORE the caller's history.commit . It clones one plain component that the font already has (the prototype), once per NewComponent , and points each detached clone at its base glyph, layer and offset. Nothing is added to the font yet. Refusals raise ValueError and name the target glyph, so a script can show a kept row: an unknown base, a base without that layer, a bad offset, and a font without any plain component ( NO_PROTOTYPE ). add_component(layer, shape) , INSIDE mutate of the caller's history.commit(..., operation="geometry") : it adds one built shape to the target layer and checks that the layer holds one more component of that base. Declare the target layers and glyphs in the commit. The caller's commit is then the ONE Undo step of the edit. NEW glyphs get their components another way: put them in the glyph's own Add Glyph data ( glyph_creation.NewGlyph(components=(Part(...), ...)) ). That works also in a font without any component, and each new glyph is its own Undo step with its components. Why no scratch glyph: a temporary glyph made with fontpr set_glyph adds an Add Glyph Undo step, and flPackage.deleteGlyph removes it outside history, so Redo would put the temporary glyph back ( flcommands.cpp:914,919 ). That path is a native milestone candidate, not shipped behaviour. The cost: an existing glyph in a font without any plain component is refused. Prototype filter: a clone copies the builder state (attached flag, attach anchor, component variation; flcompositeshapesbuilder.cpp:79-93 ) and the shape style (excluded, content lock, non-spacing, boolean operation, opacity; flshape.cpp:1906-1934,2213 ). An attached clone gets its offset overwritten at the next layer update ( fllayer.cpp:1493-1535 ). So a prototype qualifies only when every one of these reads as the default through Python; _qualifies holds the rules: the bound flShape members ( pyflshape.cpp:438-443 ): excluded and contentLocked are the bool False , opacity is 1.0; the fontpr get_glyph VFJ of its glyph ( mcptools_source.cpp:58-79 , a bound Python call; no flShape member reads these fields): the layer's elements match the layer shapes one to one; the element of the prototype has no locked , nonSpacing , booleanOperation , opacity or excluded key with a non-default value, and its component holds only glyphName , layerName and attached: false (no attachAnchor , no off2026Variation ; tags of bin_types.cpp:383,535-545 ; writers flshape.cpp:826-831 , flcompositeshapesbuilder.cpp:1141-1170 ). Anything that cannot be read, or reads otherwise, disqualifies the shape. No qualifying prototype gives the NO_PROTOTYPE kept row. Not measured natively: that a clone of a component is detached (own shapeData , reference count 1), that setting componentGlyph , componentLayer and transform on the detached clone re-targets it, and the Undo/Redo/save/reopen result. build_components has no auto-glyph consent: the edit runs in the caller's commit, whose history.refusal policy refuses auto layers and bases of auto composites. Offline tests prove the call order and the refusals only. This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules at load time; PythonQt, fontpr and scripting load when build_components runs. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.components.creation as component_creation import fly.ap.core.history.glyphs as history facts = history.scan_auto_facts(package) wanted = [component_creation.NewComponent("A", master) for master in package.masters] shapes = component_creation.build_components(package, "a", wanted, facts) target = package.findName("a") layers = [target.findLayer(m) for m in package.masters] def mutate(): for layer, shape in zip(layers, shapes, strict=True): component_creation.add_component(layer, shape) history.commit("Unicase", layers, [target], mutate, operation="geometry", facts=facts)

text: Shared plan, eject and write kernel of the component writer scripts. What: the Components writer scripts (Align By Anchor, Build From Recipes, Copy Offsets Between Masters, Decompose, Nested Finder, Replace Reference, Unlock Lock) share one model. A script planner turns one layer into Change rows. A row can hold one edit, which the script's Editor writes: EjectEditor (Decompose, Nested Finder) replaces a component with the parts of its base glyph, one level per press; MoveEditor (Align By Anchor, Copy Offsets) sets the offset of a component that plain_move accepts; other scripts subclass Editor . collect runs the planner on every editable layer and returns a Plan . Auto layers are listed and skipped, never edited. copy_problem gives the reason why the parts of a component cannot be copied safely, or "". It walks every base level as FontLab's builder does: a plain (not auto) base layer, affine transforms only, no composite shape that is not a component, no loop, not deeper than MAX_DEPTH . require_safe refuses the whole batch before any history exists: a glyph that owns an auto layer or is a base of one (also through other composites). apply_work writes all edits through ONE history.commit with operation="geometry" . EjectEditor builds the copies first, gives each removed component with its data and builder as retain= ( history.component_history ), and reads the layers back. How: eject refreshes the component cache, then copies the base parts with ejectTo() BEFORE history opens. keep_raw_state copies back what a native copy drops: the raw node connection bits (FontLab issue 8516), the element note (FontLab issue 8538) and the element name. Inside history, the write only removes the component and inserts the copies at its place. history.commit puts the retained objects first in the notification and asks for deep history, which FontLab's Undo needs for a removed component (FontLab issue 7641). Why: the logic was a private copy in each script. One App module keeps the refusals and the Undo protocol the same in every script that uses it. The generic kernel ( Change , Plan , Editor , apply_work , fmt , plural , layer_of , shown , settle ) lives in fontlabapp.masters.layers.writer ; this module re-exports it, so the Components scripts keep one import. This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules ( history , edit_guards , layer_writer ) at load time. The fontlab module loads inside the functions, so FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast. Offline tests do not prove native Undo/Redo. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.components.writer as component_writer def planner(glyph, master, layer): rows = [] for shape in component_writer.components(layer): why = component_writer.copy_problem( package, (glyph.name, master), shape, master ) edit = None if why else shape.id name = component_writer.base_of(shape) rows.append(component_writer.Change(name, "", "parts", edit, why)) return rows plan = component_writer.collect(glyphs, masters, planner) facts = history.scan_auto_facts(package) component_writer.require_safe(plan.work, facts) component_writer.apply_work( plan.work, "Decompose", facts, component_writer.EjectEditor(unlock=True) )

text: add_component ( layer : Any , shape : Any ) -> Any Add one shape from build_components to layer ; call it INSIDE mutate . Return the shape that the layer holds now ( flLayer.addShape returns it; a None answer returns shape ). Raise RuntimeError unless the layer holds exactly one more component of the same base afterwards.
title: fontlabapp.components.creation.add_component

text: build_components ( package : Any , target : str , wanted : Sequence [ NewComponent ], facts : AutoFacts , * , cache : dict [ str , Any ] | None = None ) -> tuple [ Any , ... ] Return one detached plain component per item of wanted ; call it BEFORE history.commit . target : the existing glyph that will receive them (for the texts). facts : a fresh history.scan_auto_facts(package) . Every refusal raises ValueError("<target>: kept; ...") before any change. A native failure while cloning raises RuntimeError that says nothing was added to the font (the clones are detached). Nothing wanted returns () with no native call. Pass one empty cache dict per Apply to reuse the prototype across targets in the same package. Discard the cache after Apply; a later edit can change the prototype. A missing prototype is cached too.
title: fontlabapp.components.creation.build_components

text: prototype ( package : Any , facts : AutoFacts ) -> Any | None Return the first component that qualifies as a prototype (module text), or None. Only the component users in facts.users are read, in name order, and only their non-auto layers. The VFJ elements must match the layer shapes one to one (count, and the base of each component), else the layer is skipped. Fetch each glyph VFJ at most once per call, across all layers.

text: Shared panel base and colour helpers of the component writer scripts. What: panel_type() returns ComponentPanel , the non-modal PythonQt panel of the Components scripts (Align By Anchor, Build From Recipes, Copy Offsets Between Masters, Decompose, Nested Finder, Replace Reference, Unlock Lock): script controls, a live preview table, Reload selection, Close and Apply. ink , muted and readable_palette give readable text colours in FontLab's light and dark themes. ERROR_COLOR colours blocked rows; MAX_ROWS limits the preview rows. The helpers are the same objects as in fontlabapp.anchors.panel.model and fontlabapp.metrics.panel.model . How: the panel plans with fontlabapp.components.writer ( collect , blocked_rows , require_safe ) on every control change. Apply plans again from live data, scans the auto-layer facts again and writes with component_writer.apply_work and the script's editor() (one Undo step). Signals connect through scripting.connect_guarded and disconnect in closeEvent . Why: each script then holds only its planner, a small panel subclass and main . This module imports only stdlib-only App modules at load time; PythonQt loads inside the functions, and panel_type() loads the class from fontlabapp.components.panel.ui . So FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast, and tests without Qt can import it. Offline tests do not prove native panel behaviour. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.components.panel.model as component_panel import fly.ap.components.writer as component_writer class Decompose(component_panel.panel_type()): TITLE, KEY, ACTION, DONE = "Decompose Components", "components_decompose", "Decompose", "Decomposed" HEADERS = ("Glyph · master", "Component", "Becomes") def build_controls(self): ... def planner(self): ... def editor(self): return component_writer.EjectEditor(unlock=True)

text: Pure 2D affine math in Qt's row-vector convention. No Qt import. What it does: Holds a transform as six floats (a, b, c, d, e, f) , the same order as QTransform(m11, m12, m21, m22, dx, dy) . A point maps as x' = a*x + c*y + e and y' = b*x + d*y + f . How to use: concat(first, then) applies first , then then . This is Qt's first * then . apply maps one point. invert gives the inverse. rotation makes a rotation; IDENTITY changes nothing. from_qtransform copies a native QTransform into plain floats. viewport_transform reads a FontLab canvas map as one Affine. Example: apply(concat(glyph_to_canvas, canvas_to_view), x, y) maps one glyph point to widget pixels. Why this design: - Plain tuples keep no native wrapper alive and are safe in paint code. - No Qt import. The module loads in a cold FontLab start (5 s limit) and in tests without PythonQt. Qt classes arrive as arguments. - Every public function rejects non-finite numbers with ValueError by default. A bad native matrix then fails loud, not as a silent bad paint. Pass finite=False only for deliberate raw math. Used by: canvas_rsb , canvas_anchor_rings , drawing . Glyport adopts the same names later ( fontlab_glyport.drawing.context ).

text: Contour copies and Qt path contours of the Contours generator scripts. What: Shadow Copy, Small Caps From Capitals, Superior & Inferior Figures and Tabular Figure Copies copy the contours of a layer through a transform; Outline Effect turns a stroked QPainterPath back into FontLab contours. This module holds those shared parts: contour_shapes gives the own (non-component) shapes that hold contours. copy_contours copies their contours: first the element transform, then the caller's transform. repair_nodes copies the node names and raw node flags back onto each copy. path_contours builds closed flContour objects from the elements of a QPainterPath . How: a contour copy is contour.cloneMapped(...) . FontLab's contour copy can drop node names and raw node flags (fl#8569). repair_nodes copies only these two fields back: the node names and raw node flags. Other node properties, contour names and element names and notes are not copied by copy_contours . restore_shape repairs a whole detached shape, including its shape-data name/note and contour names. It keeps clone selection bits by default; keep_view_state=True restores source selection and active flags. Why: the code was a private copy in five scripts. contour_shapes is not fontlabapp.contours.writer.outline_shapes : that one returns the shapes that an outline script may edit in place, and it keeps shared and scaled shapes out. A copy can use those shapes too, because it maps every contour through its element transform. This module imports only the standard library at load time. path_contours loads fontlab and PythonQt when it runs, so FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast. Offline tests do not prove native FontLab behaviour. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.contours.copy as contour_copy copies = contour_copy.copy_contours(layer, move) # read before history

text: Measure the vertical extent of a layer from its outline nodes. What: vertical_extent(layer) returns (ymin, ymax) of every contour of every shape of layer , or None when no contour has a node. Why: FontLab keeps flLayer.boundingBox and flShape.boundingBox as a cache. After a Python node move, the cache stays stale, also after notifyChangesApplied (fl#8575, FontLab 9.0.9790). This module never reads a boundingBox and never calls update() , so the read has no side effects. How: each shape's contours are mapped through shape.transform (an affine QTransform, read through m11() … m33() ), so a component counts at its placement, as in masters.layer_contours . Shapes without contours (stickers, empty shapes) give nothing. Nodes come from contour.nodes() as node.x , node.y and their kind: node.isOn() (on-curve), node.isCurve() (cubic control, flNode::Curve ) or else a quadratic control ( flNode::Off , node.isOff() ; flnode.h). The kind decides each segment, not contour.isTT : FontLab sets isTT when any node is a quadratic control, so one contour can mix both kinds (flcontour.cpp). As in FontLab's contour enumerator (flconturenum.h), an implied on-curve midpoint lies only between two consecutive Off nodes. Each segment between two on-curve nodes gives its end y values and its exact y extremes: the roots of the cubic derivative in (0, 1) for two Curve controls, or the one extreme for one Off control. A closed contour also gives its closing segment. Not counted, by design: stroke thickness ( maxThickness , which flShape.boundingBox adds), because zones measure the outline; and the per-contour contour.transform() , which is identity outside an interactive transform (flshapedata.cpp).

text: Shared plan kernel of the outline writer scripts (Contours folder). What: the Contours writer scripts (Round Coordinates, Remove Overlap, Add Extremes, Correct Contour Direction, Straighten Short Curves, Optimize Start Points, Delete Small Contours, Fix Zero Handles, Delete Duplicate Contours, Transform, Slant) share one model. A script planner turns one layer into Change rows; the script's Editor writes them through apply_work (one Undo step). This module adds the outline parts to the generic fontlabapp.masters.layers.writer kernel and re-exports that kernel: outline_shapes gives the own contour shapes that a script may edit in place, and a note for every shape that it keeps (shared outline data, scaled or rotated shapes). note_rows turns the notes into rows. node_points and translation read nodes and plain shape moves. collect runs the planner on every chosen layer. A glyph that the geometry policy refuses is listed and skipped as a whole; the other glyphs are still written. With compatible , a glyph whose structure edits would differ between masters is held back ( held_back ). require_safe is a compatibility hook; apply_work discloses queued glyph updates through history (FontLab issue 8537). How: a Change.key names a structure edit (for example the index of a deleted contour). held_back compares the keys of all masters: the masters stay compatible only when every master gets the same keys and every master with a key edit is in scope. Why: the logic was a private copy in each of the eleven scripts. The refusal policy differs from component_writer on purpose: an outline batch skips each refused glyph, with a row that says why, and asks for consent ( allow_bases ) before it edits bases of automatic composites. This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules ( history , edit_guards , layer_writer ) at load time, so FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast. The panel base is in fontlabapp.contours.panel.model . Offline tests do not prove native Undo/Redo. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.contours.writer as outline_writer def planner(glyph, master, layer): shapes, notes = outline_writer.outline_shapes(layer) rows = [outline_writer.Change("nodes", "3", "4", ("nodes", shapes))] return rows + outline_writer.note_rows(notes) plan = outline_writer.collect(glyphs, masters, planner, facts) outline_writer.require_safe() outline_writer.apply_work(plan.work, "Example", facts, ExampleEditor())
title: fontlabapp.contours.writer

text: Shared panel base and colour helpers of the outline writer scripts. What: panel_type() returns OutlinePanel , the non-modal PythonQt panel of the Contours writer scripts: script controls, the master scope, a "Keep masters compatible" tick for scripts that change the node structure, a consent tick for bases of automatic composites, a live preview table, Reload selection, Close and Apply. ink , muted and readable_palette give readable text colours in FontLab's light and dark themes. ERROR_COLOR colours blocked rows; MAX_ROWS limits the preview rows. The helpers are the same objects as in fontlabapp.anchors.panel.model . How: the panel plans with fontlabapp.contours.writer.collect on every control change. Apply plans again from live data, scans the auto-layer facts again and writes with outline_writer.apply_work and the script's editor() (one Undo step). A new scan clears the consent tick, because the consent belongs to the glyphs that the user saw. Signals connect through scripting.connect_guarded and disconnect in closeEvent . Why: each script then holds only its own logic, a small panel subclass and main . OutlinePanel is its own class, not a subclass of fontlabapp.components.panel.model 's ComponentPanel : the scope, the ticks, the per-glyph refusal, the error display of Apply and the status texts differ, so a subclass would replace almost every method. This module imports only stdlib-only App modules at load time; PythonQt loads inside the functions, and panel_type() loads the class from fontlabapp.contours.panel.ui . So FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast, and tests without Qt can import it. Offline tests do not prove native panel behaviour. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.contours.panel.model as outline_panel import fly.ap.contours.writer as outline_writer class RoundCoordinates(outline_panel.panel_type()): TITLE, KEY, ACTION, DONE, UNIT = "Round Coordinates", "outlines_round", "Round", "Rounded", "item" def build_controls(self): ... def planner(self): ... def editor(self): ...

MEMBERS lists the other public members a script may use, for example slot_error , status and apply_button . See fontlabapp.contours.panel.ui.OutlinePanel for the full contract. text: Shared panel base of the Contours scripts that work on the selected glyphs. What: panel_type() returns SelectionPanel , the non-modal PythonQt panel of Shadow Copy, Outline Effect, Autohint Selected Layers and Remove PostScript Hints: script controls, a master scope ("Current master" or "All masters"), a consent tick for bases of automatic composites ( BASES_TEXT ), a preview table, a status line and the buttons Use selection, Close and the action. fontlabapp.glyphs.copies.panel_type() returns CopiesPanel , the same base set up for the scripts that create glyph copies. How: the panel binds to the font that is current when it opens and takes the Font window selection. The public facts attribute stores auto-layer facts from construction, reselect() or scan() (explicit Refresh). Use self.facts in plan_rows to avoid a whole-font scan for each control signal. Every control change plans again with the script's plan_rows and fills the table with its cells . The action plans again from the live font and calls the script's write once. Use selection reads the selection again and clears the consent tick, because the consent belongs to the glyphs that the user saw. A refusal ( ValueError , RuntimeError or TimeoutError ) in Use selection or in the action shows its text in the status line. Signals connect through scripting.connect_guarded and disconnect when the panel closes. Why: the four panels differed only in their controls, so each script now holds only its own logic, a small panel subclass and main . The panel is not fontlabapp.contours.panel.model 's OutlinePanel : that one plans outline_writer rows; these scripts plan their own rows. MAX_ROWS is the fontlabapp.anchors.panel.model limit. This module imports only stdlib-only App modules at load time; panel_type() loads the class from fontlabapp.contours.selection.panel.ui , which imports PythonQt. Offline tests do not prove native panel behaviour. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.contours.selection.panel.model as selection_panel class ShadowPanel(selection_panel.panel_type()): TITLE, KEY, ACTION = "Shadow Copy", "generate_shadow", "Add Shadow" def build_controls(self): ... def plan_rows(self, package, masters): ... def cells(self, row): ... def pending(self, todo): ... def write(self, package, rows): ... def result_text(self, result): ...

text: Shared transform writer and preview of Contours > Transform and Slant. What: both scripts apply one affine matrix to the chosen layers. transform_changes plans one layer: one row for its shapes and one row for its anchors. TransformEditor writes the plan; bakes decides per shape how. layer_outline , mapped , outline_path and fit feed the before/after preview. panel_type() returns TransformPanel : the OutlinePanel of fontlabapp.contours.panel.model plus an outline preview of the first glyph that may change. How: every shape gets the composed transform (old shape transform, then the matrix). A shape that bakes accepts then gets shape.applyTransform() : FontLab writes the new nodes and resets the matrix. This is FontLab's own per-shape rule of the layer transform ( fllayer.cpp:6957-6978 ): it bakes only own contour shapes that only move, whose data no other shape shares and that include no other shapes, and composes every other shape. The write never calls layer.applyTransform : the one-argument Python binding also moves the guides, scales the advance and moves every anchor. Anchors move in place, only when the user asks. An existing anchor that would land on 0, 0 blocks Apply: anchor_writer.on_origin is the shared Redo rule (FontLab issue 8527), here with a tolerance of ORIGIN_NEAR because FontLab may round the stored point. The read-back accepts the same tolerance for rounded nodes and anchors. Why: Transform and Slant used private copies of this code. This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules ( affine , anchor_writer , outline_writer ) at load time. PythonQt loads inside the functions, and panel_type() loads the class from fontlabapp.contours.transform.ui , so FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast. Offline tests do not prove native Undo/Redo. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.contours.transform.model as outline_transform class Slant(outline_transform.panel_type()): def preview_matrix(self, layer): return matrix, guide_y def planner(self): return lambda glyph, master, layer: outline_transform.transform_changes( layer, matrix, True, "250" ) def editor(self): return outline_transform.TransformEditor()

The rule is anchor_writer.on_origin : the new point counts with the ORIGIN_NEAR rounding tolerance, the old point only when it is exactly 0, 0. text: Public queue disclosure and refusal guards for scripts that write to the current font. What: queue disclosure for ordinary writers, and four checks that raise ValueError before any native write. require_selection_window(package_id) : the active panel is a Font window of the bound font (FontLab issue 8528: selection writers crash while a Glyph window is active). require_no_editors() : no Glyph editor is open, also an inactive one (the Unicode save-cache gap of the duplicate-Unicode writer). require_settled() : FontLab has no queued native glyph updates (FontLab issue 8537: queued cache updates become semantic edits later). require_history_scope(glyphs, creates=...) : no Glyph window is the active canvas, or every owner glyph is in that canvas and no glyph is new (FontLab issue 8573: from a Glyph window, the Undo step covers only the glyphs that the canvas shows). fontlabapp.core.history.glyphs.commit , fontlabapp.glyphs.creation.create_glyphs and the eight App writers that call notifyChangesApplied directly call it. How: the selection and editor guards delegate to the reviewed private implementation ( scripting._require_selection_window , duplicate_unicodes_capture.require_no_editors ); require_settled reads the native queue once; require_history_scope reads the text blocks of the active canvas once. The implementations load only when a guard runs, so this module imports only the standard library and FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast. Why: scripts must not import private App names. Use these guards through fly.ap.core.edit_guards . fontlabapp.core.history.glyphs.commit discloses the queue by default; settled=True explicitly opts into refusing it. Never normalise unrelated dates. Offline tests do not prove native behaviour.
title: fontlabapp.core.edit_guards

text: canvas_glyphs ( native : Any = None , * , deadline : float | None = None ) -> frozenset [ tuple [ int , str ]] | None Return the glyphs that the active Glyph window shows, or None . None : no Glyph window is the active canvas, so FontLab records package history. Otherwise return one (package id, glyph name) pair for each glyph in the text blocks of the active canvas. Use the name, not the id: CurrentGlyph().id and the canvas slot id of the same glyph differ on 9790 (412 against 531175085312). These are the glyphs that FontLab's canvas history attaches an Undo step to ( flhistorycontroller.cpp , the in_glyphs branch; FontLab issue 8573). Empty slots are skipped. deadline is a time.monotonic() instant (default: now plus CANVAS_SCAN_SECONDS ); a later checkpoint raises TimeoutError . Native read errors propagate. A fontlab module without flWorkspace , or a workspace without getActiveCanvas (offline doubles), has no canvas: return None . FontLab's own module always defines both.

text: require_history_scope ( glyphs : Sequence [ Any ], * , creates : bool = False , native : Any = None ) -> None Refuse a write that FontLab would undo only in part (FontLab issue 8573). While a Glyph window is the active canvas, FontLab attaches the Undo step of notifyChangesApplied only to the glyphs that this canvas shows. Other notified glyphs keep the change after Undo (measured on 9790). With the Font window active, the Undo step covers every notified glyph. glyphs : the owner glyphs of the write, matched by font and glyph name. creates : the write makes new glyphs (a new glyph is never in the canvas). Raise ValueError(CANVAS_TEXT) before any write when a Glyph window is the active canvas and the write creates glyphs, or when an owner is not in the canvas. When the canvas cannot be read, use the safe rule: allow no owner, or one owner that is the current glyph, and no new glyph. With no active canvas, return. Call it on the GUI thread only; other threads are refused. native is the fontlab module (default: the native one).

Raise ValueError for an open or unreadable editor and TimeoutError when the widget scan passes the deadline. The scan reads only the inherits("GlyphWindow") predicate, with cyclic GC off.

text: One native Undo step for a script edit, with auto-layer refusals. What: commit runs a script's font change as ONE FontLab Undo step, in the order that the reviewed App writers use: Refuse before any write ( ValueError , nothing touched): queued native glyph updates only with settled=True (FontLab issue 8537; otherwise disclose them); optionally a missing Font window or an open Glyph editor (Unicode writers); a Glyph window as the active canvas when an owner glyph is not in that canvas (FontLab issue 8573: the Undo step would cover only the shown glyphs; see edit_guards.require_history_scope ); an auto layer in the edit list or among the retained objects; a glyph that the operation policy refuses. checkInitHistoryState(0) on every layer, then every glyph. mutate() . It may return the new native objects it made (for example new layers); they join the notification after the declared layers. One shared UTC lastModified stamp on every glyph. ONE notifyChangesApplied(title, layers + created + glyphs) . With retained objects: ONE notifyChangesApplied(title, retain + layers + created + glyphs, True) . The same stamp again: window observers re-stamp after the history capture. read_back() : the caller compares the font with its plan. Retained objects ( retain= ): a script that removes a component gives the ORIGINAL shape, its shapeData and the builder, read BEFORE the removal ( component_history(shape) ). They go first in the notification, before the layers, and the third argument True asks for deep history. Glyport does the same ( fontlab_backend._retain_component_history and _notify ): its docstring says FontLab 9784 needs this to restore a removed component on Undo (fl#7641). Without retain the call is the two-argument call, unchanged. Steps 4 to 6 run also after a failed mutate , so a partial edit stays on the Undo stack. Every failure is collected and raised as PartialWriteError (a RuntimeError ) whose text says "Native changes may remain; use Edit > Undo". No rollback is tried: Edit > Undo is the recovery. Why the refusals: notifying a list that holds an auto layer makes FontLab re-resolve every default-recipe auto layer in the font, and a change to a base glyph rebuilds its auto composites. Anchors and locks can change and Undo does not restore them (measured; see the workspace AGENTS.md). The policy depends on the operation: "rename" , "unicode" , "geometry" : refuse glyphs that own an auto layer and glyphs that are a base of an auto composite (also through a chain of manual composites). allow_bases=True lets a base through after the user agreed to the rebuild; an auto owner is never let through. "metadata" (notes, tags, mark colours): refuse only glyphs that own an auto layer. How to use:: import fly.ap.core.history.glyphs as history facts = history.scan_auto_facts(package) result = history.commit( "Round Advances", layers, glyphs, lambda: edit(layers), operation="geometry", facts=facts, read_back=check, ) report(result.mismatches) The module imports only the standard library at load time; FontLab modules and fontlabapp.guides.inspect.model load when a function runs. Offline tests prove the call order only, not native Undo/Redo/reopen behaviour.

text: One native Undo step for font-level edits on one or more masters. What: commit_masters writes master values (zones, vertical metrics) as ONE FontLab Undo step. It uses route A of the issue 122 M2 measurement (FontLab 9.0.9790): the history objects of Font Info and "Sync font metrics" ( dlgfontinfo.cpp:2100-2175 , mainwindow_edit.cpp:1208-1226 ): Refuse before any native write ( ValueError ): a thread other than the GUI thread; no active Font window of this font, or a Glyph window as the active canvas (measured in the Font window only); an unknown, duplicate or empty master list; an empty title. Read the queued glyph ids once ( edit_guards.pending_updates ). Never clear them. checkInitHistoryState(0) on the package and on ONE package.mastersContainer() handle. For each requested master, in font order: setMaster(name, False) , read() and save() (the values to restore), write() , read() again and verify() that value. setMaster(original, False) . ONE flItems().notifyChangesApplied(title, [package, container], False) . No glyph and no layer is in the list, so no auto layer is notified. Rollback policy (a decision that differs from history.commit ): history.commit always notifies, also after a failure, and Edit > Undo is the recovery. Here a failure in steps 3 to 5 (a write callback error, or a read-back mismatch) comes BEFORE the notification. So the helper restores every master that it touched, in reverse order, reads each one back, and notifies nothing. Edit > Undo would revert the user's previous step, so no error text recommends it. An interrupt ( KeyboardInterrupt , SystemExit ) also runs the rollback and the master restore, then is raised unchanged. All values restored: raise RolledBackError (a ValueError : the font is as before, like a refusal). A caller whose restore re-creates native objects passes restored_text to say so ( zone_native ). A restore failed, or the notification failed: raise UnrestoredError (a history.PartialWriteError ). Values can remain with no Undo step. Known host defect (fl#8574, measured on 9.0.9790, issue 122 M2): after Edit > Undo or Redo of such a step, both masters show only 3 of the 9 font-metric guidelines (the zone guidelines) until package.updateFontMetrics() runs or the font is reopened. The saved file is correct. This module does not patch Undo; it cannot hook the user's Undo. How to use:: import fly.ap.core.history.masters as font_history edit = font_history.MasterEdit(save, write, read, verify, restore) result = font_history.commit_masters(package, "Edit Zones", {"Bold": edit}) edit_guards.disclose(result) The module imports only the standard library at load time. Offline tests prove the call order only, not native Undo/Redo/reopen behaviour.

text: commit ( title : str , layers : Sequence [ Any ], glyphs : Sequence [ Any ], mutate : Callable [[], Iterable [ Any ] | None ], * , operation : Operation , facts : AutoFacts , allow_bases : bool = False , read_back : Callable [[], Iterable [ str ]] | None = None , settled : bool = False , window : int | None = None , native : Any = None , stamp : Any = None , retain : Sequence [ Any ] = (), glyph_window_ok : bool = False ) -> Committed Run mutate as ONE native Undo step. See the module text for the order. title : the Undo name. layers : every existing layer that mutate changes (all layers of a glyph for renames and Unicode). glyphs : their owner glyphs. mutate() : the edit; return new native objects to notify, or None . operation and facts : the refusal policy ( facts from a fresh scan_auto_facts ). allow_bases : let bases of auto composites through after the user agreed. read_back() : return one text per mismatch between font and plan. settled : refuse queued native updates (explicit opt-in; default False discloses pre-write ids in Committed.pending_updates without clearing them). window : the bound package id; when given, run require_selection_window and require_no_editors first (Unicode writers). native / stamp : the fontlab module and the UTC stamp; the defaults are the native module and QDateTime.currentDateTimeUtc() . retain : native objects to keep in the Undo state, first in the list, with the deep-history flag True (use component_history for each removed component, read before the removal). They get no checkInitHistoryState and are not in Committed.created . Empty: the two-argument notification, as before. glyph_window_ok : skip the Glyph-window check ( edit_guards.require_history_scope ). Use it only for a caller that a native test proves safe; no caller uses it now. Raise ValueError before any history call for a refusal. Raise PartialWriteError when anything fails after history started, including a new auto layer from mutate (it stays out of the notification).

text: component_history ( shape : Any ) -> tuple [ Any , ... ] Return the native objects to retain when a script removes shape . When: call it BEFORE removeShape , outside mutate . Glyport records that a builder read after detachment can already be too late (fl#7641). text: launch ( path : str | Path ) -> dict [ str , Any ] Run a relocated script beside its resources and retain its globals. Ordinary scripts run as main . Rescued ports use build(qt) with the preserved part1 host/ownership helpers; their live handle is returned under rescued_handle and reused until closed. No QApplication is created. Retained GetGo entries bind their original examples namespace explicitly; an already loaded foreign namespace is refused before executing the entry. Only cwd and sys.path are restored; script effects and exceptions propagate.

Names follow action identity, never visibility or menu position: among siblings whose labels give the same name, the one whose objectName slug is that name keeps it, else the smallest objectName, else the first entry without one. text: font_id ( package : Any ) -> int Return the font_id that FontLab's fontpr tools need for package . What: int(package.fgId) , the FontGate id of the package. Why: fontpr finds a font by its FontGate id ( MCPTools::findPackage -> flWorkspace::findPackageId compares fgId , source mcptools.cpp:1025-1035 , flworkspace.cpp:1278-1287 ), and get_fonts reports that id. package.id is a different id (the flObject id). With package.id a tool fails with "Font id not found", or, when the ids collide, reads or writes ANOTHER open font. Use: fontpr.call("get_font_info", font_id=scripting.font_id(package)) . Keep package.id for current_package(expected_id) and the other identity guards; those compare flPackage.id .

text: disconnect_connections ( connections : Connections , report : Callable [[ Exception ], Any ]) -> None Pop in reverse order; report ordinary failures and continue draining. Only the specified slots are disconnected. A failed pair is already popped, matching the compatibility callers' existing behavior. A report failure or BaseException propagates immediately, leaving unattempted pairs available. A report that adds pairs makes them part of the same drain; callers must not continually reconnect while closing. Repeated teardown of an empty list is harmless. A timeout detaches the current queue before processing it in insertion order. Work scheduled during processing belongs to a fresh batch; nested event loops can dispatch that batch immediately. The caller must retain any dispatch-depth refusal and error sink it needs. Processor failures propagate unchanged and abandon the unattempted detached tail, matching the donor.

text: Explicit sources and destination folder; one run at a time. Start validates every job in FontLab first (Fontport's run() is eager) and writes nothing on failure. The work then runs in a separate Python 3.11+ with fontlab-fontport (python=..., else $FONTLABAPP_BATCH_PYTHON), so it never holds FontLab's GIL; each 50 ms poll reads at most 64 KiB and records at most 64 rows from a non-blocking pipe. Output that is not a result row stops the run visibly. Cancel stops before the next font. Close (including parent or own-widget destruction) cancels and returns at once; batch_worker.supervise then collects the child (terminated after GRACE_SECONDS, killed later; a terminated font can leave a partial destination), removes its scratch files and deletes the hidden, detached panel. Outputs are named -transformed.ufo and never replace a file.

text: read_feature_blocks ( package : Any ) -> dict Read exact ordered VFJ feature source through Fontport and fontpr. Requires an active registered font inside FontLab (fontpr is host-provided). Native object ids guard the UI binding; fgId identifies the fontpr font. Raise ValueError when the bound font is no longer the active font.
title: fontlabapp.fontui.feature_blocks.read_feature_blocks

text: write_feature_blocks ( package : Any , expected : dict , updated : dict , * , references : Iterable [ str ], undo_name : str ) -> dict [ str , int ] Apply an exact source-bound feature plan with Fontport's history checks. All referenced glyphs and the complete source snapshot must still match. Fontport validates split-back, language synthesis and empty history slots before mutation, and notifies only package/features. Groups are untouched. Unexpected native errors may leave partial changes; they are not hidden. Refuse with ValueError when the font is inactive, the source differs from expected , or a referenced glyph is gone. Return {"changed": 0} when expected == updated and {"changed": 1} after a write. The master that was active before the write is restored in finally .
title: fontlabapp.fontui.feature_blocks.write_feature_blocks

text: follow_changes ( owner , callback , fonts , delay_ms = CHANGE_DELAY_MS ) Call callback after FontLab reports changes; return signals connected. Connected whenever FontLab is present (nothing outside it); fonts() is read at each signal, so an owner whose fonts appear later starts following then. Signals count only while fonts() holds a FontLab-backed font, and glyph(s)Updated only for those documents. The first signal arms a single-shot timer that later signals never restart, so callback runs at most delay_ms after the first change even under a steady stream. Signals emitted while any follower's callback runs (refresh reads or writes, also from other open controls) are ignored, no callback is re-entered, and a timer that fires during another follower's callback runs after it. Before it, each FontLab-backed (Fontport) font is refreshed, which drops its loaded glyph and layer handles. owner.close() disconnects everything; a pending timer then fires into nothing.
title: fontlabapp.fontui.lifecycle.follow_changes

text: follow_history ( owner , callback ) Call callback after FontLab's Undo/Redo actions; return connections made. FontLab connects its own handlers first, so ours run after the history step. Outside FontLab (no fontlab module) nothing is connected. owner.close() disconnects these like every other owned connection.
title: fontlabapp.fontui.lifecycle.follow_history

text: Shared kernel of the scripts that make new glyphs from copies of existing ones. What: Small Caps From Capitals, Superior & Inferior Figures and Tabular Figure Copies plan one new glyph per selected source glyph and copy its contours, transformed, into every master. This module holds the parts that were byte-identical in the three scripts: survey_with plans one Row per selected name with the script's naming rule. It lists and skips a repeated target, a missing source, a target that exists, a source layer that cannot be copied ( source_problem ) and, without the user's consent, a target that can make FontLab rebuild automatic glyphs ( Row.rebuild ). create makes the planned glyphs through fontlabapp.glyphs.creation.create_glyphs : each glyph with its master widths, then all contours in one Undo step, then a read-back. panel_type() returns CopiesPanel , the shared panel of the three scripts (a fontlabapp.contours.selection.panel.model panel with a source table and the rebuild consent tick). How: a job is (new name, [(master, contours, advance)]) ; the script's prepare builds it with fontlabapp.contours.copy.copy_contours . Undo: glyph_creation.UNDO_TEXT . This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules at load time; PythonQt loads in panel_type() and fontlab in create . Offline tests do not prove native Undo/Redo. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.glyphs.copies as glyph_copies rows = glyph_copies.survey_with(package, names, naming, facts, allow_rebuild) result = glyph_copies.create(package, jobs, "Small Caps", facts, allow_rebuild=True)
